slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did God promise Jesus as the lamb? Abraham tells Isaac that God will provide a lamb. A ram is then killed instead of Isaac. John later calls Jesus “the Lamb of God.”
slides.body: Abraham tells Isaac that God will provide a lamb. A ram is then killed instead of Isaac. John later calls Jesus “the Lamb of God.”
slides.heading: Did God promise Jesus as the lamb?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Gen 22:8: Abraham answered, ‘God Himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.’
slides.body: Abraham answered, ‘God Himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.’
slides.heading: Gen 22:8

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Jn 1:29, BSB: The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, “Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!
slides.body: The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, “Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Jn 1:29

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Why Christians connect them A beloved son faces death, but God provides another victim in his place. Christians see this as a powerful preview of God giving Jesus to save others.
slides.body: A beloved son faces death, but God provides another victim in his place. Christians see this as a powerful preview of God giving Jesus to save others.
slides.heading: Why Christians connect them

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But the story gives its own answer God provides a ram for that day’s sacrifice. John never says he is referring to Isaac’s story, and his lamb image could come from several other Bible passages.
slides.body: God provides a ram for that day’s sacrifice. John never says he is referring to Isaac’s story, and his lamb image could come from several other Bible passages.
